title: Which Frank Beverage appears in the 1937 wedding photograph?
status: Two conflicting identity trails; exact relationships unresolved
summary: A 1939-dated Thomaston plot card and a 1954 North Haven self-reported birth inscription cannot describe the same man if their dates are correct. The 1937 photo belongs to a Frank-and-May couple, but their exact identification is not yet proved.
known: The 1937 Calderwood diary records a 50th wedding anniversary for Frank and May on October 15 and mentions a photograph caption; an October 1887 wedding is a strong inference, not yet confirmed by a marriage register.

The contemporary October 18, 1930 Courier-Gazette NORTH HAVEN column reports the couple celebrated their 43rd wedding anniversary on Wednesday October 15. This independently corroborates the 1937 diary's fiftieth-anniversary date, strengthening October 15, 1887 as the commemorated marriage date, not yet a certified marriage return.
A historical 1954 autograph-album transcription reports a North Haven Frank Beverage born January 14, 1861.

The Thomaston Village Cemetery lot table records a different Frank with a February 5, 1939 card date and includes an Orra S. Roney burial. A 1911 newspaper reports an Orra Roney visiting a Frank Beverage Green Street household.
The existing North Haven Frank profile already records work as a butcher, hides dealer, treasurer and auctioneer from independent documents.
unresolved: The 1939 cemetery-card date may be an interment date, not a certified date of death.
Whether the 1911 Green Street household is the cemetery Frank and how Orra Roney was related are not yet documented.
No original October 1887 marriage return or May's maiden name is established.
The 1937 original photo is mentioned in the diary transcript but has not been located or licensed.
next_records: Find an original October 1887 marriage return for Frank and May in North Haven/Vinalhaven area registers; establish both full names.
Obtain original Thomaston cemetery plot card or a 1939 death certificate to identify the 1939 Frank and distinguish his relatives.
Obtain a digital photograph of the autograph-album signature (with access permission if applicable) and search for the original 1937 anniversary photo.
Identify 1911 Green Street municipality via the newspaper's page heading and historical household census.

title: Who were Nathaniel Beverage's parents?
status: 1865 family established as a published account; parents and uncle relationship unverified
summary: Eaton's 1865 history supplies Nathaniel's Rockland household and says Nathaniel and Sarah Alexander were Matthew's nephew and niece. A derivative genealogy proposes John White Beverage and Rachel Crosby, introducing a generational contradiction if Capt. Matthew was Capt. Thomas's brother.
known: Eaton printed Nathaniel's Rockland residence, occupation as carpenter, spouse Sarah Alexander and their three children Henry T., Mercy and Frederic.
The published genealogy gives Henry T.'s birth as November 29, 1841.
An 1898 marriage index cited in FamilySearch links a Henry T. Beverage to Ella Allen; the original marriage document has not been inspected.
Nathaniel born around 1804 is not Nathaniel Winslow Beverage born in 1776.
unresolved: John White Beverage and Rachel Crosby are only proposed parents in a derivative family tree.
The claim that Capt. Matthew was a direct son of James Beveridge has not been established.
If the candidate genealogy is correct, Nathaniel may be Matthew's grandnephew rather than nephew; both source interpretations need testing.
The marriage between Nathaniel and Sarah, their reported birth information, and Capt. Matthew's probate remain to be checked against civil or probate records.
next_records: Locate the 1838 Nathaniel Beverage/Sarah Alexander marriage entry in Maine registers, or explain why it cannot be found.
Search John White Beverage and Rachel Crosby probate inventories and guardianships for a Nathaniel child.
Check Rockland/Thomaston 1850–1880 original federal census pages for Nathaniel and his household.
Await the previously requested Waldo County probate search for Capt. Matthew; verify the actual estate record if identified.

title: Where were the original Beverage bridges, dams and properties?
status: Historic bridges and landowners documented; family acreage and deed chains not resolved
summary: The 1848 Maine bridge law gives a contemporaneous landowner reference. A society exhibit reproduces an 1883 bridge contract naming Alvin Beverage and reports an 1888 Harrison dam purchase. None of these alone defines an ancestor's full parcel boundary.
known: Maine's official 1848 bridge law locates an authorized bridge route near land of James and Josiah Beverage at the head of Pulpit Harbor.
The Historical Society's bridge exhibit reproduces a town contract involving Alvin Beverage, connected to the 1883 Beach Bridge account.
A separate Mill Stream history reports Harrison Beverage's 1888 dam purchase; its original deed has not been retrieved.
Knox County deed indexes cover the 1888 period; Maine provides an official county registry portal.
unresolved: The index entry and book/page for the 1888 dam conveyance have not been identified.
Alvin's complete name, parentage and genealogical connection are not established.
The rescued Pulpit Harbor map, deed papers and bridge bills discussed in the 1975 historical society account have not been individually cataloged here.
No surveyed boundary or acreage for these specific ancestral parcels is verified.
next_records: Search Knox County grantor and grantee indexes around 1888 for Harrison Beverage/Beveridge and identify the corresponding deed book/page and original legal description.
Use the bridge exhibit to extract original Alvin contract parties and names; request the original from the society only after separate approval.
Identify the institution's 1975 salvaged-map inventory, box or call numbers and compare with digitized early plats.
Map parcels only after original deed boundaries, identifiable landmarks and a georeferenced historical survey can be reconciled.

title: Who were the James Beveridge and Jean White in the 1749 intention?
status: Marriage intention reported by two transcriptions; individual identity and marriage not independently verified
summary: The same Brunswick register appears in 1888 and 1895 publications with different spellings and Old Style dates. These are a path to an original record, not separate proof of two couples or a marriage ceremony.
known: An 1888 transcript lists James Beveridge and Jean White of Georgetown, intention dated February 6, 1749.
An 1895 transcript renders them James Beviridge and Jean Write and dates the entry February 6, 1748–9.
The transcriptions almost certainly derive from the same town record; neither is an original solemnization record.
unresolved: No original manuscript image of the marriage intention has been inspected.
No church or town marriage return has independently established that the couple married.
Identifying this James and Jean with existing historical ancestors and early Topsham lot holders remains a hypothesis.
next_records: Locate the Brunswick marriage-intentions manuscript and confirm the original spellings and Old Style date convention.
Search contemporary Georgetown/Topsham church register marriage returns, estate records and land transfers for the same pair.
Document the linkage to James Jr., Jean McKinney White and the family tree only if the independent records support it.
